pr.title: Store the type of each GVN value
pr.description:
MIR is fully typed, so type information is an integral part of what defines a value. GVN currently tries to circumvent storing types, which creates all sorts of complexities.

This PR stores the type along with the enum `Value` when defining a value index. This allows to simplify a lot of code.

Fixes rust-lang/rust#128094
Fixes rust-lang/rust#135128

issues.body:
### Code

```Rust
#![allow(unused)]

pub trait Foo {
    fn test(&self);
}
async fn generic_function<'g, X: Foo>(x: &'g X) {}

where
    i32: Foo,
{
    V,
}

where
    i32: Foo;

    i32: Foo,
{
}

where
    i32: Foo,
{
    f: i32,
}

where
    i32: Foo,
= ();
impl Foo for ()
where
    i32: Foo,
{
    fn test(&self) {
        3i32.test();
        Foo::test(&4i32);
        generic_function(5i32);
    }
}
async fn f()
where
    i32: Foo,
{
    let s = S;
    3i32.test();
    Foo::test(&4i32);
    generic_function(5i32);
}
async fn use_op<'g>(s: &'g String) -> String
where
    String: ::std::ops::Neg<Output = String>,
{
    -s
}
async fn use_for()
where
    i32: Iterator,
{
    for _ in 2i32 {}
}
trait A {}
impl A for i32 {}
struct Dst {
    x: X,
}
struct TwoStrs(str, str)
where
    str: Sized;
async fn unsized_local()
where
    Dst<dyn A>: Sized,
{
    let x: Dst<dyn A> = *(Box::new(Dst { x: 1 }) as Box<Dst<dyn A>>);
}
async fn return_str() -> str
where
    str: Sized,
{
    *"Sized".to_string().into_boxed_str()
}
async fn global_hr<'g>(x: &'g fn(&()))
where
    fn(&()): Foo,
{
    x.test();
}
fn main() {}
```

analysis.originalLogic: GVN interned only a structural `Value` and reconstructed the MIR type when needed from compact metadata such as `AggregateTy` and `Value::Cast { from, to }`. Its value identity therefore did not include the type, so two occurrences with the same structural value description could be treated as the same value even when their MIR types differed. Const evaluation then recomputed layouts from those reconstructed types, including inside coroutine bodies. The PR states: "MIR is fully typed, so type information is an integral part of what defines a value. GVN currently tries to circumvent storing types, which creates all sorts of complexities."
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation was type-erasing GVN/CSE: treat a structural `Value` alone as the complete identity of an interned value, identify occurrences that differ only in MIR type, and later reconstruct the type from the value shape (`AggregateTy::Array/Tuple/Def/RawPtr`, `Cast { from, to }`, `ProjectionElem` type payloads) before interpreting it. That is unsound because the type is part of the value, and reconstructing/evaluating layouts of malformed or nonsensical types can ICE. The fix changes the interning key to `FxIndexSet<(Value<'tcx>, Ty<'tcx>)>` and replaces type-carrying value variants with type-free variants plus the stored type, e.g. `Aggregate(VariantIdx, Vec<VnIndex>)`, `RawPtr { pointer, metadata }`, `Projection(VnIndex, ProjectionElem<VnIndex, ()>)`, and a cast variant holding only `kind` and `value`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies processed by GVN, especially async/coroutine bodies; rvalues involving aggregates, raw-pointer construction, casts, projections, ZSTs/transmutes, `PtrMetadata`, and constants. The relevant cases include structurally identical values whose MIR types differ, and bodies with malformed or nonsensical types (for example an erroneous coroutine body, or trivial bounds such as `str: Sized`) where recomputing a layout during GVN evaluation is invalid or cycles.
analysis.trigger:
GVN interns/compares a value without its type and then either (a) reuses it in a context with a different type, or (b) reconstructs its type from the value representation and calls layout/evaluation machinery. The newly tracked trigger for the layout-cycle ICE is evaluating a non-scalar type's layout while inside a coroutine body: the patch adds `is_coroutine: body.coroutine.is_some()` and the guard `// Avoid computing layouts inside a coroutine, as that can cause cycles.` with `let ty = if !self.is_coroutine || ty.is_scalar() {`.

Focused paired inputs can differ by the type attached to the same structural value: e.g. a unit/ZST value versus a different ZST such as `Never`, or `PtrMetadata` on a thin raw pointer (metadata `()`) versus a wide pointer (metadata `usize`). A second pair can use an ordinary well-formed body versus a malformed coroutine/nonsensical-bound body compiled with GVN enabled.
analysis.summary: Historical GVN bug fix: GVN stored structural values without their `Ty`, so its value identity ignored the fact that MIR is fully typed. The PR makes the interning key `(Value, Ty)` and derives projections/casts from the stored type, fixing ICEs in malformed coroutine layouts (#128094) and nonsensical-sized-str bodies (#135128). Regression expectations also change for ZST transmute folding and `PtrMetadata` of thin pointers.
preconditions: GVN must run, e.g. via normal optimization or `-Zmir-enable-passes=+GVN`; the regression test uses `//@ compile-flags: -Zmir-enable-passes=+GVN` and another uses `-Copt-level=1`.
The body must contain a value whose type is not safely recoverable from its structural GVN representation, or a type whose layout must not be recomputed during GVN evaluation.
For the coroutine-layout ICE class, the body is a coroutine/async body, including malformed bodies reached during error recovery.
For the nonsensical-bound ICE class, the body contains trivial/nonsensical bounds such as `str: Sized`.
pitfalls: Do not intern or compare GVN values without their MIR types: two structurally equal `Value`s can belong to different types and are not interchangeable.
Do not reconstruct an aggregate/raw-pointer/cast type from the value shape; store the `Ty` alongside the value and read it back.
Inside coroutines, avoid computing layouts for non-scalar types because that can cause query cycles; the patch explicitly guards `layout_of` with `!self.is_coroutine || ty.is_scalar()`.
Handle ZSTs before interpreting structural contents: the patch folds a typed ZST to `ImmTy::uninit(ty)`, and the MIR expectation changes to `// CHECK: = const ZeroSized: Never;`.

Be careful with `PtrMetadata`: the regression comment says `// Metadata usize -> (), do not optimize.` and the expected MIR for the thin-pointer case becomes `const ()` rather than retaining `PtrMetadata(copy ...)`; metadata type must come from the stored pointer type.
Raw pointers are represented specially as a pointer/metadata variant so they are not treated as ordinary field-bearing aggregates; metadata and mutability checks depend on tracked types.
Only mark an SSA local reusable when the local type and assigned rvalue type match exactly; the retained FIXME notes `rvalue` may have a subtype of `local`.
Mutation/assignment invalidation matters: the patch checks `lhs.is_indirect()` and invalidates derefs on indirect assignments, rather than assuming all non-empty projections are mutating uses.
analysis.testStrategy: Use MIR-opt tests under `tests/mir-opt/` with `//@ compile-flags` and explicit `CHECK`/diff expectations to verify type-sensitive folding. The patch updates `tests/mir-opt/const_prop/transmute.rs` and both 32-bit/64-bit GVN diffs to expect `const ZeroSized: Never` for `transmute(())` to `Never`, and updates `tests/mir-opt/gvn.rs` plus `gvn.generic_cast_metadata.GVN.{panic-abort,panic-unwind}.diff` around `PtrMetadata`, including the comment `// Metadata usize -> (), do not optimize.`. Add UI regression tests for the two ICE classes: `tests/ui/mir/gvn-nonsensical-coroutine-layout.rs` with `//@ compile-flags: -Zmir-enable-passes=+GVN` and expected type errors, and `tests/ui/mir/gvn-nonsensical-sized-str.rs` with `//@ compile-flags: -Copt-level=1`, `//@ build-pass`, and the expected `trivial_bounds` warning. Pair programs that produce the same structural value at different types (ZST vs other ZST, thin vs wide pointer metadata) and assert they are not merged; separately compare a well-formed body with a malformed/nonsensical-type body. No compiler was built or executed for this analysis.
evidence: MIR is fully typed, so type information is an integral part of what defines a value.
This PR stores the type along with the enum `Value` when defining a value index.
